item.description: Do research agents have taste, the judgment of which experiments are worth running before their outcomes are known? We give six frontier models seven recent NLP papers. item.title: Ask HN: Are you tired too in this AI era?
item.description:
Although AI lets us do much more, I feel considerably more tired than before.

We need to keep track of many things happening in parallel and read enormous amounts of generated text. The constant guardrailing, decision making, and context switching overload me.

I am pretty sure most of you are experiencing the same as me, but: Have you found ways of using AI without increasing mental overload?

I would love to hear your tips, but still be relevant in this AI era, so my boss does not fire me. — 来源：arxiv · reddit_ml · github · verge_ai · hackernews — 原文：https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50301479

item.description: Luggage re-identification (ReID) is a critical task in video surveillance for forensics, security or border management (suspicious or abandoned luggage recognition), as well as luggage management (lost luggage recovery). item.title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
item.description: Data attribution methods for Language Models (LMs) are typically evaluated using downstream tasks like fact retrieval. However, existing evaluations vary multiple dataset properties simultaneously, making it impossible to isolate exactly why an attribution algorithm fails. To diagnose these failures, we explore the design space of LLM data attribution, with a primary focus on evaluation. item.title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations
item.description: The Neural Thickets hypothesis posits that pretrained language models lie in dense neighborhoods of task-specific experts in weight space, which random Gaussian perturbations can uncover. We reproduce the reported gains, but show that they do not require this geometric explanation. item.description: In film editing, every frame matters. While macro, content-level edits shape the high-level narrative of a film, small local edits often control timing and direct visual attention. For example, editors can adjust the precise timing of clips to control the length of a meaningful silence, or cut to shots that highlight a specific character's reactions to important moments. item.description: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) hedges data-driven two-stage stochastic programs against error in the distribution estimated from a finite record, and standard ambiguity sets differ in how they treat realizations absent from that record. A divergence ball around the empirical distribution contains only reweightings of the record, whereas a transport ball also contains distributions supported off the record, including on realizations the data-generating process cannot produce, against which the decision is then hedged as well. item.description: The marginals of a continuous diffusion model can be reproduced by a deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE), known as the probability flow ODE, which provides a foundation for accelerated sampling and consistency distillation. In this paper we address the question whether an analogous formulation exists for discrete diffusion models and answer it affirmatively by introducing exponential residual flows (ERFs). item.title: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
item.description: Safety alignment has enabled large language models to reliably refuse harmful requests directly, yet the same request distributed across a multi-turn conversation still succeeds far too often. This brittleness has a mechanistic root: Alignment is shallow, with safety behavior concentrated in a model's first few output tokens, and existing defenses inherit the weakness, supervising the surface form of the response without ever giving the model an explicit safety decision to learn. item.title: world2vec: Mechanistic world models through latent dynamics learning
item.description: World models can achieve strong control performance without faithfully capturing the dynamics of their environment, limiting their potential for mechanistic interpretability and scientific discovery. Here, we introduce world2vec to learn mechanistic world models without reward information directly from observations and actions. item.description: As robots and intelligent systems increasingly interact with humans, they must anticipate long sequences of future actions from only brief observations. While purely neural models typically require extensive observations to predict future actions and remain difficult to interpret and adjust, symbolic priors offer a structured alternative. item.description: Visual grounding is crucial for robots to understand language instructions with visual observations. Prevailing methods derive uncertainty from the VLM itself. item.description: Recent progress in visual scene generation has extended beyond static 3D scenes toward the more challenging problem of generating dynamic 4D scenes from minimal input. item.title: From extreme weather to agricultural consequences with agentic AI
item.description: Extreme weather is forecast days ahead, yet its consequences for agriculture remain hard to predict: a forecast says where a storm will strike, not which crops will suffer or how much is at risk, and the records that could tell span many sources. We present WxCrop, the first agent that judges agricultural hazards from physically interpretable weather indices examined by causal analysis, and the first that combines weather and agricultural information to predict crop loss reliably for past and forecast dates. item.title: Difficulty Calibration Across Time for Membership Inference in Diffusion Models
item.description: Modern diffusion models are trained on massive datasets that often include copyrighted or private images. The standard approach scores an image by its reconstruction loss and flags low-loss images as members. item.description: Interactive world models generate visual content conditioned on user actions, yet maintaining spatial consistency over long-horizon exploration in real time remains challenging. item.description: We present TextSeal2, a distortion-free watermark for large language models that keeps its signal under speculative decoding: tokens that replace rejected drafts remain watermarked with the same keys, and the acceptance rate is unchanged. item.description: Proactive assistants offer short, memory-grounded hints during a conversation, deciding when to assist and what to suggest. item.description: A playable, programmable game world must maintain persistent state, enforce executable rules, and support extensible gameplay mechanics. item.description: When AI agents share channels and credentials, one agent can press another to break its operator's rule, a first step towards collusion. item.description: An autonomous research laboratory could conduct an entire study, from formulating questions to preparing manuscripts. item.description: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) is limited by sparse outcome-level feedback on hard reasoning tasks: when all rollouts in a group fail, rewards provide no learning signal. item.description: Fine-grained action annotations can support skill reuse and compositional generalization in robot policies. item.description: Current zero-shot anomaly detection methods often rely on complex prompt-learning techniques or computationally expensive sliding-window strategies to achieve fine-grained visual alignment to detect small-scale anomalies. item.description: Building and scaling computer-using agents (CUAs) across desktop, mobile, and web environments requires reliable task-completion verification for data curation, evaluation, and reinforcement learning. item.description: Clinical genomic analysis requires experts to integrate evolving guidelines, databases, and computational evidence. item.description: Realistic, fast robotics simulations could enable large-scale training of embodied AI models that transfer to the real world. item.description: This study investigates the capabilities of Large Language Models to simulate counselling clients in educational role-plays in comparison to human role-players. item.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
item.description: Foundation models are typically trained in stages: pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL), with changes in both data and learning algorithms.
